Who changed a row since the round last applied it

log_change_authors.Rd

The people whose writes to an intent field stand between the round's last execution of the row and now, newest first. The last execution is the newest event that wrote applied_seal, which the round writes only when it has applied the row, and with the channel's account configured only an event of the channel counts, log_executions(): what came before it was carried out already, under somebody's responsibility, and is not the change the round is now asked to carry out. Where the row's log no longer holds that event the whole history counts, which can only ask for an approval more often.

Usage

log_change_authors(
  events,
  record,
  fields = register_intent_fields(),
  channel_account = NULL,
  current = NULL,
  creator = NULL,
  approvers = character()
)

Arguments

events

The event log, as register_log() returns it.

record

The record id to look at.

fields

The intent fields. Passed in by a caller that asks about many rows, since deriving them reads the packaged dictionary.

channel_account

The REDCap usernames that hold the round's token, one or more, or NULL when they are not configured, for log_channel_accounts().

current

The row as the round will leave it, a data frame of one row holding every field in fields, or NULL when there is no row in hand. Read only on a row the round has carried out.

creator

Who created the row, as log_creators() answers, for log_uncovered_writes(); or NULL, and then every newest write below the seal is read as the value carried out. log_pending_authors(), the one the round asks, passes it.

approvers

The IT accounts whose approval counts on any row, for log_uncovered_writes().

Value

A character vector of usernames, newest first (by the write that counts) and each once; character() when no intent field changed, or nobody but the channel changed one; NA_character_ when the log cannot say who did.

Details

Only the writes still in the row count, decided on 2026-10-17 (option (a) of three). For each intent field whose current value differs from the one carried out, the author is whoever wrote that field last; a write somebody other than the channel then overwrote is not part of the change, and a field brought back to the value carried out is no change at all. The value carried out is the newest write of the field below the seal, by anybody, the channel included; where the log holds none it is unknown, and the field counts if it was written above the seal. It is unknown as well where that newest write is one the execution did not cover, log_uncovered_writes() (decided on 2026-10-17): a change made while the round ran sits below its seal without having been carried out, and read as the value carried out it would make a third person who brings the field back to it above the seal no author at all, so the change would be carried out on the rights of somebody who did not write it. That reading needs creator, from which the owner of the stretch is read; without it the newest write below the seal is the value carried out.

The current value comes from the register and not from the log, which cuts a value at its first apostrophe and would call D'Angelo and D'Amico equal. For the same reason a value carried out that holds an apostrophe is unknown too: read D, it would make a later D look like no change.

On a row never carried out there is no value to compare with, and every intent field written in its life counts, with its last author, empty or not: an empty field decides what is granted too, an empty dag_name a user in no group, an empty expiration an access with no end. The same holds without the row in hand, current = NULL: every field written since the last execution counts, with its last author.

This is also the way out of a write by somebody who could not have made it by hand: the owner writes that field again, and the other is no longer its author. Without it a row touched by mistake would stay held for ever, since nothing is ever deleted. REDCap logs no write that leaves the value as it was, so writing again means changing the value and then putting it back.

"Carried out already" holds for what the round read, and the seal is written at the end of the round: a change made while the round ran sits below it and was not. log_uncovered_authors() looks for those, and log_pending_authors() is the two together, which is what the round judges.

The round's own writes are not a change. It writes username back when it resolves it, and username is an intent field: counted, the channel would be an author of every row whose username it settles. Its account is the one log_channel_accounts() names, and its events are dropped by account: a field only the channel wrote since the last execution carries no author. Another account's write of a field of the channel is no change either, and with the account configured it is ignored; its write of an intent field, username included, is a change of its author like any other.

Two cases make the answer unknown rather than short, and the caller holds the row on both. Without the configured account, a second account writing what only the channel is meant to write, log_channel_unknown(): the channel is guessed from those writes, and taking the wrong account for it would drop its author from the change. And a write that counts whose author is blank names nobody, which is not the same as naming the creator.
